Duration::defined¶

Back to Duration API Reference

Signature¶

bool Duration::defined() const noexcept

What It Tells You¶

defined() reports whether the handle owns duration storage. It answers a storage-state question, not whether the duration is nonzero, nonempty, or free of NaT values.

Public Duration factories always return defined objects. A scalar zero, a shape containing a zero-length axis, and an array whose lanes are all NaT are therefore all defined. Use numel() for cardinality and isnat() for lane-wise absence.

Duration currently has no public undefined factory and cannot be default constructed. The query exists because library internals and owning wrappers still need a cheap, non-throwing way to inspect handle state.

Returns¶

true when backing storage exists; otherwise false. The check is constant time, performs no allocation, and does not inspect individual lanes.

Examples¶

Example 1. A scalar produced by a unit factory is defined.

const auto value = pluss::duration::seconds(90);
std::cout << std::boolalpha << "defined=" << value.defined()
          << " dim=" << value.dim()
          << " numel=" << value.numel() << "\n";

Output¶

defined=true dim=0 numel=1

Example 2. A zero-element array is still a real, defined object.

const auto empty = pluss::duration::zeros({2, 0, 3});
std::cout << std::boolalpha << "defined=" << empty.defined()
          << " dim=" << empty.dim()
          << " numel=" << empty.numel() << "\n";

Output¶

defined=true dim=3 numel=0

Example 3. NaT is lane data, not an undefined handle.

const auto value = pluss::duration::nanos(pluss::Duration::kNaT);
std::cout << std::boolalpha
          << "defined=" << value.defined()
          << " isnat=" << value.isnat().item<bool>() << "\n";

Output¶

defined=true isnat=true

See Also¶

  • numel: distinguish allocated emptiness from scalar storage.

  • isnat: test missing lanes rather than handle state.

  • sizes: inspect the complete logical shape.
